the resonant transmission of perpendicularly polarised light through an individual subwavelength hole in a thin gold film is activated by a plasmonic coupling between the incident light and existing film plasmon resonances.

the spectral properties of a resonant transmission through a single hole in a thin metal film are determined by the coupling between the perpendicular electric field component of incident light with the existing antibonding plasmon modes in a film.

the resonant transmission of perpendicularly polarised light through a hole in a thin metal film is due to coupling between the light field and the existing film plasmon mode, and that the resonant wavelength can be tuned by varying the thickness of the film.

the study of the optical properties of a thin metal film perforated with a subwavelength hole.
the optical properties of thin films, in particular with the interaction of electromagnetic waves with metallic thin films.
the interaction of light with a thin metallic film.
